- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 2–5% to account for downward momentum.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model frequently overcorrects and overshoots; cap forecast at +10% above peak or adjust downward by 3–8% in next 3–5 days.  
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative within 3–5 days, model often fails to adjust; apply a “sentiment pivot” rule: reduce forecast by 5–10% if sentiment drops below 0.33.  
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias: if forecast is > 10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence.  
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to underestimate in bearish sentiment cycles; add 3–7% buffer if sentiment < 0.33 for 3+ consecutive days.  
- If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is trending, model often lags; forecast should be adjusted to match 1–2 day lag of actual trend.
